newsitem.title: CANADA: Weekend rain, snow key to Red River flood - Manitoba.
newsitem.headline: Weekend rain, snow key to Red River flood - Manitoba.

text.p: Weekend precipitation could determine the severity of flooding in Manitoba's Red River Valley, a Manitoba Natural Resources official said Thursday.

"We're waiting for this Colorado low (pressure system) that's supposed to dump snow and rain on us this weekend, and depending on how much we get, all the favorable weather we've had in the last 10 days may be for naught," MNR's manager of Water Planning and Development Larry Whitney said in an interview.
Twelve cm (five inches) of snow remained standing on the ground at Winnipeg International Airport Thursday compared to 43 cm (17 inches) a year ago, Environment Canada said.
The Red River Valley has seen normal seasonal temperatures in the past week and a half. Thursday's midday temperature was also at the seasonal normal of 3 Celsius (37 Fahrenheit).
"It's really too soon to say, but if we get any amount (of precipitation) we'll probably issue a forecast next Wednesday or Thursday," Whitney added.
MNR's last forecast for the Red River Valley set the flood level at one to 1-1/2 feet higher than last year's flood, based on normal spring weather.
Rapid melt or heavy spring rain could see levels three to five feet higher than 1996 between the U.S. border and Winnipeg.
Last year's flood delayed spring seeding of wheat, barley, canola, flax and corn by one month.
The fertile Red River Valley accounts for two percent of Canadian Prairie acreage but 3.5 percent of grain output, according to the Canadian Wheat Board.
Last year's flood was compounded when storm on April 20 added 11 cm (four inches) on the Red River Valley after most of the winter snow had melted, Environment Canada meteorologist Mike Russo said.
The Red River Valley was forecast to see five to 10 cm (two to four inches) of snow Friday night into Saturday, he said.
Southeast Manitoba should see five to 10 mm (0.2 to 0.4 inch) during the same storm, while Brandon and Dauphin in western Manitoba should see some snow as well, Russo added.
Significant flooding was also expected in southeast Manitoba on the Brokenhead, Whitemouth and Whiteshell rivers, MNR's last forecast said.
